title: Co-Intelligence
subtitle: Living and Working with AI
pitch: A Wharton professor's practical guide to working with today's AI as a strange new kind of colleague, with simple rules for using it well.

chapters.g: Large language models are odd: brilliant at some things, weak at others, and hard to predict.
Always invite AI to the table, be the human in the loop, treat AI like a person but tell it what kind, and assume this is the worst AI you will ever use.
Using AI as a creative partner, coworker, tutor and coach, with examples from teaching and business.
AI is uneven: inside its frontier it boosts performance, outside it can mislead.
Four scenarios, from AI stalling to fast growth, and what each means for people.

ideas: Use AI for everything you can to learn its strengths.
Keep a human in the loop.
AI's abilities form a jagged frontier.
Today's AI is the worst you will use.

args.a: Everyone should start using AI now to learn it.
args.c: Critics worry about overreliance, errors and losing skills.
Studies show both gains and harms, depending on the task and whether it sits inside the frontier.

questions: Where is the jagged frontier in your work?
Which of the four rules is hardest to follow?
What skill would you protect from AI?

quiz.q: What does the jagged frontier describe?
quiz.w: Good at some tasks, bad at nearby ones.

quiz.q: What is one of Mollick's rules?
o: Be the human in the loop
